writeup: Astronomers have identified a previously unknown eclipsing binary star system called TIC 224215371. This pair of stars orbits each other every 10.986182 days, causing periodic dimming as they pass in front of each other. The primary eclipse dims the system's light by 1.43 percent, while a secondary eclipse has also been detected. The discovery was confirmed through multiple independent methods, including detailed pixel-level analysis of telescope images. Remarkably, this system does not appear in any major variable-star catalogs, making it a genuine new find for the astronomical community.
